description: Dull brown plates shut on a copper vein, far too heavy for its size. A Puddling's last piece; in armour, hard to shift.
lore: The one they put in a new hand first. It weighs wrong — not heavy, wrongly heavy, in a way the arm reports before the eye agrees. Armour set with one does the same trick at scale: the blow that should have put you on your back leaves you standing where you were, and you find out afterwards. Wearers call it the least dramatic advantage in the trade, and keep wearing it.

The trouble is the count. Every hard piece is supposed to be [[lore/the_hard_pieces|the bottom of one long forgetting]], and the wet ground gives up more of these than the low country has lives to account for, by a margin that worsens every season. [[characters/7a779de1|Wendell]] says that in his day the count came out even. Wendell says that about most counts.

The sorters keep three explanations in stock. That the ground itself is doing the forgetting, and the wet places are where it runs deepest. That the counting was always sloppy. And a third, said late in the evening and not repeated in daylight: that the arithmetic is fine, and it is the assumption of one life to one stone that is wrong.
gm_notes: This is the ONE record that carries the whose-forgetting-is-a-made-thing-the-bottom-of puzzle; the sibling stones now defer to it instead of each retelling it. It stays unsettled — never rule between the three explanations.
